partners.mechanism_chain: BTD (HGNC:1309) —PRODUCES→ Biotin (CHEBI:15350); Biotin (CHEBI:15350) —BINDS→ Biotin-dependent carboxylase activity (GO:0009329); Biotin-dependent carboxylase activity (GO:0009329) —LEADS_TO→ Developmental delay (HP:0001263); PC (HGNC:8725) —DISRUPTS→ Pyruvate (CHEBI:16567); Pyruvate (CHEBI:16567) —PRODUCES→ Acetyl-CoA (CHEBI:16135); Acetyl-CoA (CHEBI:16135) —LEADS_TO→ Tricarboxylic acid cycle (GO:0006099); Tricarboxylic acid cycle (GO:0006099) —LEADS_TO→ Seizures (HP:0001250). Loss-of-function mutations in BTD lead to impaired biotin recycling, affecting biotin-dependent carboxylases (like pyruvate carboxylase) crucial for gluconeogenesis and energy production. Similarly, loss-of-function mutations in PC directly impair pyruvate carboxylation, a key anaplerotic reaction for the TCA cycle and gluconeogenesis. Both deficiencies converge on dysregulated energy metabolism, particularly affecting the brain, leading to shared phenotypes such as developmental delay and seizures.

### CANDIDATE DETAIL
#### 1. pyruvate carboxylase deficiency disease  —  Tier 3 — Moderate / Emerging  (fitness 0.471)
**Link type:** shared pathway (Reactome:R-HSA-196780)

**Proposed mechanism:** BTD (HGNC:1309) —PRODUCES→ Biotin (CHEBI:15350); Biotin (CHEBI:15350) —BINDS→ Biotin-dependent carboxylase activity (GO:0009329); Biotin-dependent carboxylase activity (GO:0009329) —LEADS_TO→ Developmental delay (HP:0001263); PC (HGNC:8725) —DISRUPTS→ Pyruvate (CHEBI:16567); Pyruvate (CHEBI:16567) —PRODUCES→ Acetyl-CoA (CHEBI:16135); Acetyl-CoA (CHEBI:16135) —LEADS_TO→ Tricarboxylic acid cycle (GO:0006099); Tricarboxylic acid cycle (GO:0006099) —LEADS_TO→ Seizures (HP:0001250). Loss-of-function mutations in BTD lead to impaired biotin recycling, affecting biotin-dependent carboxylases (like pyruvate carboxylase) crucial for gluconeogenesis and energy production. Similarly, loss-of-function mutations in PC directly impair pyruvate carboxylation, a key anaplerotic reaction for the TCA cycle and gluconeogenesis. Both deficiencies converge on dysregulated energy metabolism, particularly affecting the brain, leading to shared phenotypes such as developmental delay and seizures.

**How to falsify it:** If genetic analysis reveals that variants in BTD or PC are not loss-of-function, or if studies show no significant overlap in the metabolic consequences of biotin deficiency and pyruvate carboxylase deficiency on shared downstream pathways like the TCA cycle, this hypothesis would be falsified. _(variant: rs121918440 (a known pathogenic variant in BTD) is found at a frequency > 0.001 in gnomAD.)_

**Why it matters:** Understanding the shared metabolic vulnerability in biotinidase deficiency and pyruvate carboxylase deficiency could lead to novel therapeutic strategies. For instance, adjunctive biotin supplementation in PC deficiency, or improved understanding of substrate accumulation in BTD, could offer avenues for treatment beyond current supportive care.

#### 2. propionic acidemia  —  Tier 3 — Moderate / Emerging  (fitness 0.453)
**Link type:** shared pathway (Reactome:R-HSA-196780)

**Proposed mechanism:** Biotinidase (HGNC:1206) —DISRUPTS→ Biotin (CHEBI:16797); Biotin (CHEBI:16797) —DECREASES→ Biotinylation (GO:0015745); Biotinylation (GO:0015745) —LEADS_TO→ Developmental delay (HP:0001251); Propionyl-CoA carboxylase alpha subunit (HGNC:9194) —DISRUPTS→ Propionyl-CoA (CHEBI:17340); Propionyl-CoA carboxylase beta subunit (HGNC:9195) —DISRUPTS→ Propionyl-CoA (CHEBI:17340); Propionyl-CoA (CHEBI:17340) —DECREASES→ Propionate Metabolism (GO:0006097); Propionate Metabolism (GO:0006097) —LEADS_TO→ Metabolic acidosis (HP:0002066). Both disruptions lead to distinct but overlapping metabolic disturbances and downstream phenotypic consequences.

**How to falsify it:** Demonstration that the genetic variants identified in BTD patients do not impact biotinidase activity or that variants in PCCA/PCCB do not impair propionyl-CoA metabolism. _(variant: rs749174905 (missense variant in BTD with reported low frequency))_

**Why it matters:** Understanding the shared metabolic pathway disruptions can inform therapeutic strategies, potentially including cofactor supplementation or metabolic interventions, for patients with these distinct but mechanistically linked disorders.

**Link type:** shared pathway (Reactome:R-HSA-196780)

**Proposed mechanism:** BTD (HGNC:1423) —DECREASES→ Biotin (CHEBI:17676); Biotin (CHEBI:17676) —DISRUPTS→ Biotinylation of carboxylases (GO:0006689); MCCC2 (HGNC:7403) —DECREASES→ 3-methylcrotonyl-CoA (CHEBI:17157); 3-methylcrotonyl-CoA (CHEBI:17157) —DISRUPTS→ Propionate metabolism (REACT:R-HSA-168958); Biotinylation of carboxylases (GO:0006689) —LEADS_TO→ Developmental delay (HP:0001263); Biotinylation of carboxylases (GO:0006689) —LEADS_TO→ Hypotonia (HP:0001252); Propionate metabolism (REACT:R-HSA-168958) —LEADS_TO→ Developmental delay (HP:0001263); Propionate metabolism (REACT:R-HSA-168958) —LEADS_TO→ Hypotonia (HP:0001252); Propionate metabolism (REACT:R-HSA-168958) —LEADS_TO→ Seizures (HP:0001250); Propionate metabolism (REACT:R-HSA-168958) —LEADS_TO→ Metabolic acidosis (HP:0010977); Biotinylation of carboxylases (GO:0006689) —LEADS_TO→ Metabolic acidosis (HP:0010977). #### 4. 3-methylcrotonyl-CoA carboxylase 1 deficiency  —  Tier 3 — Moderate / Emerging  (fitness 0.444)
**Link type:** shared pathway (Reactome:R-HSA-196780)

**Proposed mechanism:** BTD (HGNC:1264) —DISRUPTS→ Biotin (CHEBI:15743); Biotin (CHEBI:15743) —PRODUCES→ Biotinyl-CoA (CHEBI:17487); Biotinyl-CoA (CHEBI:17487) —BINDS→ Biotin-dependent carboxylases (GO:0004435); Biotin-dependent carboxylases (GO:0004435) —LEADS_TO→ Hypotonia (HP:0001252); MCCC1 (HGNC:7204) —DISRUPTS→ 3-methylcrotonyl-CoA (CHEBI:17717); 3-methylcrotonyl-CoA (CHEBI:17717) —PRODUCES→ 3-methylglutaconyl-CoA (CHEBI:17718); 3-methylglutaconyl-CoA (CHEBI:17718) —PRODUCES→ Propionyl-CoA (CHEBI:16120); Propionyl-CoA (CHEBI:16120) —BINDS→ Biotin-dependent carboxylases (GO:0004435); Biotin-dependent carboxylases (GO:0004435) —LEADS_TO→ Developmental delay (HP:0001263). **How to falsify it:** Demonstration that the downstream metabolic effects of biotin deficiency on biotin-dependent carboxylases are entirely independent of the effects of propionyl-CoA accumulation on these same enzymes, or identification of a specific genetic variant in MCCC1 with a pathogenic frequency >1% in gnomAD that explains the entirety of MCCC1 deficiency cases, thus ruling out a broader metabolic link. _(variant: rs74315301)_

#### 5. acetyl-coa carboxylase deficiency  —  Tier 3 — Moderate / Emerging  (fitness 0.438)
